Ingredion's chief executive approached Penford in July 2014; after a secrecy agreement, Ingredion floated $17.00 per share on 08/06 and sent an $18.00 cash indication of interest on 08/10. Penford's board, advised by Deutsche Bank and Perkins Coie, refused exclusivity, gave Ingredion a management presentation and diligence access, sounded out its 9.28% holder SEACOR, which was not interested, and on 08/28 authorized a market check. Deutsche Bank contacted six strategic parties: Party A, which had approached Penford in August, and Parties C and D signed confidentiality agreements, Parties B and F declined, Party E never responded, and the board chose not to approach Party G. After repeated feedback that the board wanted $20.00, Ingredion moved to $18.25–$18.50, then $18.50, then $19.00 on 10/02, and on 10/03 the board directed definitive negotiation with Ingredion while Party D dropped out and Party C did not move forward. Party A, encouraged to submit a letter, indicated a value below $17.50–$18.00, cut its range to $16.00–$18.00 and on 10/14 sent a $16.00 letter, citing market volatility. Ingredion confirmed $19.00 despite weaker draft fiscal 2014 results, and the parties signed on 10/14 with a SEACOR voting agreement and announced the merger on 10/15.
